chapter.title: Memory
chapter.para: A guest sees a memory of its own: its RAM and the devices that the hypervisor gives it.

section.para: The hypervisor shall map the RAM of a VM into the physical address space of its guest by nested page tables on x86_64 (from address 0 up to the size of the memory) and by stage 2 translation tables on arm64 (from address 0x40000000), with the memory of the host as its backing.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Address translation by the processor is what keeps a guest in its region.

section.para: The hypervisor shall map nothing into the physical address space of a guest but the RAM of its VM and the devices that this document gives to the guest.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Address translation by the processor is what keeps a guest in its region.

section.para: The hypervisor shall stop a VM, and only that VM, whose guest accesses memory outside its RAM that is not a device that the hypervisor gives to it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest that touches memory that it does not have is faulty.

section.para: The hypervisor shall give the guest on arm64 the devices that the VM needs by mapping their pages as device memory, not executable: the virtual interface of the interrupt controller, and the registers of a UART that the guest uses directly.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Some devices are used by the guest without the intervention of the hypervisor.

section.para: The hypervisor shall write the data cache back to memory and drop the instruction cache over the RAM of a VM on arm64 when it loads the VM, because the guest starts with its MMU and caches off.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The guest would otherwise execute stale code.

section.para: The hypervisor shall use, for itself, memory that it maps with its own translation: with the MMU on, an identity map, on arm64.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The hypervisor itself needs a defined memory map.
